best_for: Windows developers starting with Rust, or juggling stable and nightly across projects, who want the official installer that keeps the compiler and Cargo up to date.

points.title: The official way to get Rust
points.text: The Rust project calls rustup the preferred install method. It installs rustc, cargo and the other tools, switches between stable, beta and nightly, and updates them with `rustup update`.

points.title: You may need Visual Studio's build tools
points.text: The default Windows toolchain links with Microsoft's tools, so the installer may ask you to install the Visual Studio C++ Build Tools. A GNU toolchain is the alternative, but many crates then need a full MSYS2 and MinGW setup.

points.title: Per-project versions
points.text: A `rust-toolchain.toml` file in a repository pins its toolchain, components and targets. `rustup override set` does the same for a folder without touching the repo.

points.title: Cross-compiling targets
points.text: `rustup target add` downloads prebuilt standard libraries for other platforms. One Windows toolchain can build for all four x86 Windows targets.

points.title: Lives in your profile
points.text: Tools go into `%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin`, which is added to your PATH. To use other folders, set `CARGO_HOME` and `RUSTUP_HOME` before running the installer and keep them set.

points.title: Removing it
points.text: `rustup self uninstall` removes Rust and rustup completely.

points.title: Windows only here
points.text: This page lists `rustup-init.exe` for x86, x64 and Arm64 and keeps 12 versions. On macOS and Linux the project installs rustup with a one-line `curl` script instead.
